patch.layout: rows = forward (row 0 is 8 cells behind the rover), columns = left..right, 5 m cells
patch.normalisation: height - rover height / 10 m; slope / 20 deg; roughness / 1 m; clipped to +-10

scalars.normalisation: speed / v_cap; heading error / pi; distance to waypoint / 100 m (<= 10); sun azimuth relative / 180 deg (0 at night); shadow flag

card.title: Behaviour-cloned rover driver (PilotNet-style CNN, DAgger against the scripted expert)
card.intended_use: stochastic generator of driving times / interventions for the LunarSim driving tables
card.limitations: trained on one terrain pack; kinematic rover on 5 m LOLA heights (90 % interpolated); lighting is a speed/shadow model, not imagery; interventions are rule-based (env.py)

evaluation_note: Recomputed 2026-10-16 (B-18) from the saved ONNX, without retraining. The first evaluation (env version 1) counted an intervention loop: on PSR->PAD_A@3 at night the planned route crosses a 20 m cell above the 0.5 m roughness limit, and version 1 put the rover back on the route at or next to that cell after each intervention, so it intervened on (almost) every step until the 50,000-step cap: about 46,000 interventions and 3,900 h for one drive, i.e. hundreds per km overall. Env version 2 resumes past the hazard (one intervention per hazard, as in the driving tables). Every other drive had 0-1 interventions in both versions. Definitions: interventions/km = interventions / distance driven (km); route_km = planned route length; time_h = elapsed time incl. stops and intervention costs; autonomy % = 100 (1 - interventions x (RTT + 300 s recovery) / elapsed time); RTT 4 s for both levels (it sets the intervention cost; the autonomous level has no stops); 50,000-step limit per drive. The training record (env version 1, incl. its DAgger rollouts, which contained the same loop) is unchanged.
